The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Utla Gangadhar ,
Goondla Ganga Boi on 20 June, 2023

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Utla Gangadhar ,
Goondla Ganga Boi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: Lalitha Kanneganti
Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 The Honourable Smt Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.No.3607 of 2008
 and
 Ma Cma No.1943 of 2009
Common Judgment:
Since both these appeals arise out of the same award, they are being disposed of by this common judgment.

2. M.A.C.M.A.No.3607 of 2008 is preferred by the claimants aggrieved by the award and decree dated 02-04-2008 in O.P.No.1711 of 2002 on the file of the I Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Nizamabad.

entities.text: I Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: M.A.C.M.A.No.1943 of 2009 is filed by the Insurance Company questioning the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and its liability.

3. Heard learned counsel for the claimants Mr. L. Dayakar Reddy and learned counsel for the Insurance Company Mr. P. Harinath Gupta and perused the record.
4.

The brief facts are that on 20-03-2002, while the deceased Utla Galavva @ Gangavva was travelling in a trailer bearing No.AP-25-T-750 attached to Tractor bearing No.AP-25-T-749 from Domaledgi Village to Rudrur Village, as a labourer and when the tractor reached in the limits of Rudrur Vilage, its driver drove the same at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the 2 LK, J MA CMA.No.3607 of 2008 & 1943 of 2009 scooterist, who was going ahead, thereafter, the driver of tractor lost control over it and it turned turtle, due to which the deceased received multiple and grievous injuries to her head and died on the spot.
The claimants have filed OP., claiming compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in the accident.

5. Respondent-Insurance Company filed counter denying the manner of accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the crime vehicle and the death of the deceased, her age, avocation and income.
It is stated that the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the scooter by its rider and the owner and insurer of the scooter are necessary parties to the claim petition.
It is stated that the amount claimed is highly excessive.

6. The Tribunal on analyzing the oral and documentary evidence gave a finding that as per the charge sheet-Ex.A1, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the tractor and The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Utla Gangadhar , Goondla Ganga Boi on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175940822/
1 granted compensation of Rs.3,14,000/- with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Utla Gangadhar , Goondla Ganga Boi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that while computing the compensation, the Tribunal has not considered all the heads and the compensation that was granted is not reasonable.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the policy is an Act policy and the vehicle is insured for non-agricultural purpose and as per the policy, only the driver of the vehicle was covered.
He submits that even if assuming that there are labourers, the labourers are not covered as per the policy and once they are not covered, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
9. In this factual backdrop, the point that arises for determination is whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal to the claimants is just and proper.

10. Coming to the liability of the Insurance Company, according to the Insurance Company, the deceased was travelling as gratuitous passenger and as per the claimants, she was travelling as labourer at the time of accident.
This Court has perused the policy.
It is an Act policy and the premium was paid only to the driver and the vehicle is for non-agricultural purpose and no premium was paid for the labourers for the purpose of loading and unloading.

The Honourable Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Prembhai Patel 1 , in similar set of facts, has held that as per the policy, as it is an Act liability, the Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation arising under the Workmen's Compensation Act and the Insurance Company and the owner of the vehicle are liable to satisfy the award.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Prembhai Patel 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the deceased was aged about 48 years.
According to the claimants, she was a labourer working on contract basis and doing vegetable business and also milk vendor and cultivating her own lands and earning a sum of Rs.12,000/- per month.
But the Tribunal considering the deceased as housewife, took her monthly income at Rs.3,750/- and granted compensation.

As per the law laid down by the Apex Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited 2 , even in case of a daily labourer, the Apex Court has taken monthly income at Rs.4,500/- without any evidence and in this regard, a sum of Rs.4,500/- can safely be taken as monthly income of the deceased and if half of the amount is deducted, it comes to Rs.2,250/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per Section 4-A of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923,
where the death results from the injury, an amount equal to fifty per cent of the monthly wages of the deceased workman multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount of Rs.80,000/-, whichever is more has to be taken.
As per Schedule-IV, for the age of the deceased as 48 years, the multiplier is 159.80.
Then, the loss of income due to dependency comes to Rs.2,250/-x159.80=3,59,550/-.

Thus,
a sum of Rs.3,59,550/- is granted to the claimants for the death of the deceased in the accident.

(2011) 13 SCC 236 5 LK, J MA CMA.No.3607 of 2008 & 1943 of 2009 The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Utla Gangadhar , Goondla Ganga Boi on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175940822/
2 12.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimants have relied on the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in V.Mekala v. M. Malathi and another3 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court, taking into consideration the date of the accident and till the appeal reached to the Apex Court, has awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards cost of litigation.

entities.text: V.Mekala v. M. Malathi and another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards cost of litigation.

13. In the light of the above discussion, the claimants are entitled for compensation under the following heads;
1. Loss of dependency -- Rs.3,59,550/-
2. Legal expenses -- Rs. 10,000/-
 ____________  Total: Rs.3,69,550/-
 __________ 14.
In the result, MA CMA No.1943 of 2009 is partly allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.3,14,000/- to Rs.3,69,550/-.
(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(b) The respondent-Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

On such deposit,, the claimants are permitted to 2014 (5) ALD 42 (SC) 6 LK, J MA CMA.No.3607 of 2008 & 1943 of 2009 withdraw the compensation as apportioned by the Tribunal without furnishing any security.
15. M.A.C.M.A.No.3607 of 2008 filed by the Insurance Company is partly allowed.
No order as to costs.
16. Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending in both the appeals shall stand closed.
_ _ _ SMT LALITHA KANNEGANTI, J 20th June, 2023.
sj The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Utla Gangadhar , Goondla Ganga Boi
